title: The effects of resveratrol on human health | 2019, Volume 5 - Issue 4 | Demiroglu Science University Florence Nightingale Journal of Medicine
abstract:
The most recent experimental data has reported that resveratrol may be beneficial in protecting against diabetes and alleviating some diabetic complications. It was indicated that resveratrol improved metabolic parameters, decreased plasma glucose and triglyceride concentrations, and reduced the effect of insulinemia in diabetes-induced rats. It was also reported that it may prevent oxidative stress-related nephropathy caused by diabetic hyperglycemia.\[[28](#r28)]  
Preclinical data showed that resveratrol may be helpful in management of diabetes by improving insulin resistance and problematic insulin signalization and preventing pancreas beta cell apoptosis and dysfunction.\[[27](#r27)]
1\. Vascular compliance and blood pressure  
Intake of 2.5 mg/kg/day of resveratrol over 10 weeks increased small mesenteric artery compliance and reduced wall stiffness in normotensive rats. Resveratrol therapy weakened arterial compliance in hypertensive rats by inhibiting extracellular kinase-regulated signaling.\[[37](#r37)]  
Resveratrol had no effect on low blood pressure in low doses, while at higher doses of 200 mg/kg/day, resveratrol together with hydralazine was more effective in lowering blood pressure in naturally hypertensive rats compared to resveratrol or hydralazine alone.\[[17](#r17)]  
Resveratrol had no effect on blood pressure at low doses (2.5 mg/kg/day for 10 weeks); high-dose resveratrol of 200 mg/kg/day lowered systolic blood pressure in hypertensive rats. Combination of low-dose resveratrol (2.5 mg/kg/day) with hydralazine (25 mg/kg/day) was more effective than resveratrol or hydralazine alone in lowering blood pressure in hypertensive rats. Likewise, a meta-analysis of six randomized control studies in humans showed that resveratrol intake of 150 mg/day reduced systolic blood pressure, but not at doses any lower.\[[17](#r17)]  
To date, there are few studies on the effect of resveratrol on blood pressure in humans. In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study, high-dose resveratrol (125 mg twice daily) was shown to reduce both systolic and diastolic blood pressure, while lower dose of 50 mg twice daily had no effect.\[[38](#r38)]
In one randomized placebo-controlled clinical study, in which resveratrol was initiated at 500 mg daily dose for 52 weeks and later increased to 1000 mg twice daily dose, it was reported that it was safe and well-tolerated by Alzheimer’s patients. In that study, the resveratrol group had significant decreased levels of Aβ in CSF and plasma compared to the placebo group. However, other significant biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease were unaffected. Therefore, the study concluded that it could not clearly demonstrate the effect of resveratrol on Alzheimer’s disease.\[[47](#r47)]  
To the contrary, 200 mg/day resveratrol for 26 weeks and 320 mg/day quercetin supplementation (to improve bioavailability of resveratrol) improved memory performance of adults with healthy weights.\[[48](#r48)]
